entry.title: Bruce Wayne's Guide to Effective Employee Retention
entry.summary:
Author: thisisannabanana

Rating: Teen And Up AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 23,030Chapters: 2/11Kudos: 34

Summary: Bruce Wayne has contingency plans for alien invasions, compromised allies, hostile gods, and the destruction of Gotham. He does not have one for Ligaya Avila handing him her resignation. -or- Bruce looked at her desk, the abandoned coffee, the Gotham Knights mug, the stack of completed briefings. “I don’t know what I’d do without you.” There it was. Warm. Sincere. Thoughtless. Aya stood. She picked up the cream envelope and placed it in his hand. “You’ll have to find out.” —or— After seven years of managing Bruce Wayne’s schedule, secrets, and disasters, Aya is finally ready to build a life of her own. Bruce takes this as a problem to solve. A slow-burn workplace romance featuring mutual pining, a family with no respect for privacy, and one increasingly personal employee-retention strategy.

Rating: Teen And Up AudiencesLanguage: EnglishWords: 165,996Chapters: 42/?Kudos: 5,273

Summary: Gotham was literally cursed but no one believed Bruce. He took it upon himself to fix it and after decades of searching, that solution came to him in the form of a little blue vial. Bruce was to take the curse within himself to temper it into something manageable.He thinks the others would call him stupid and stop him if they knew about this, but (un)fortunately for Bruce, his family hasn't spoken to him for forever. There was no one here to stop him.He downed the liquid and woke up as his nine-year-old self.Ch3 Excerpt:“Mother, do you remember those funny clouds above people’s heads I told you about? Well, I’m doing something about them but the process is very lonely. Or not. I think it’s just me. I’m the problem. I can’t seem to get people to like me enough to stay. I know–-… I’m aware that it’s due to my own shortcomings but sometimes, it feels like even the worst monsters have people that love them and yet I have no one.”Bruce let out a humourless chuckle and rested his forehead on his knees.“I just wish there was someone that cared about me.”

Summary: Love was not a matter of agreement, or even shared values. That is how it is with family: you can clash and argue and fight, but no one else can. No one else has the right to. And even after a thousand disagreements and even more arguments, Bruce remained the man who raised them. The man who grew into the role of a father for every kid that had lived under this roof. So if this alternative Bruce had no Robins, one could at least hope there was someone else waiting for him. Someone who thought of him beyond just Batman. It was only fair, for no Bruce should ever be alone. Even if Bruce himself most often did not realize so. Bats are social creatures, after all.
